issue_context.title: /healthz?verbose=true should report component timings
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:
Getting `/healthz?verbose=true` from apiserver presently returns output like:
```
[+]ping ok
[+]log ok
[+]etcd ok
[+]poststarthook/generic-apiserver-start-informers ok
[+]poststarthook/start-apiextensions-informers ok
[+]poststarthook/start-apiextensions-controllers ok
[+]poststarthook/bootstrap-controller ok
[+]poststarthook/rbac/bootstrap-roles ok
[+]poststarthook/scheduling/bootstrap-system-priority-classes ok
[+]SSH Tunnel Check ok
[+]poststarthook/ca-registration ok
[+]poststarthook/start-kube-apiserver-informers ok
[+]poststarthook/start-kube-apiserver-admission-initializer ok
[+]poststarthook/start-kube-aggregator-informers ok
[+]poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller ok
[+]poststarthook/apiservice-status-available-controller ok
[+]poststarthook/apiservice-openapi-controller ok
[+]poststarthook/kube-apiserver-autoregistration ok
[+]autoregister-completion ok
healthz check passed
```

It would be nice if each of these lines included a statement of how long that check took to run.

**Why is this needed**:
We were debugging a cluster with inexplicably slow /healthz responses today and knowing why/what was slow would have been helpful.
comments:
I like this idea, I would like to take this one. I was thinking that we could simply add the time in the end of each line, for example:

```
[+]ping ok 15ns
[+]log ok 1.739µs
[+]etcd ok 2.5s
```

The implementation seems pretty straight-forward, just time each check in the handler `handleRootHealthz` at the file `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/healthz/healthz.go`.

If we don't want to add this directly maybe could add another request parameter.

Could anyone validate?
it's unclear if the output of that endpoint is supposed to be considered machine-parseable. if so, we might need a separate parameter to include timing info
Yes, that is what I was afraid. We could add a `includeTime` parameter?
Or perhaps ?verbose=trace so as not to introduce a new parameter. (Especially since including the timings is not meaningful when !verbose.)
a distinct value for the verbose parameter seems reasonable

> Or perhaps ?verbose=trace so as not to introduce a new parameter. (Especially since including the timings is not meaningful when !verbose.)

Alternatively, we can output timings in outputted logs when includeTiming query param is set. This would mean that we can decouple the two query params and customize the behavior for verbose output when the two are both present. 

It makes using healthz with query params a bit simpler and more intuitive since we can do this:

`curl localhost:8080/healthz?verbose&includeTimings`
`curl localhost:8080/healthz?verbose`
`curl localhost:8080/healthz?includeTimings`

> @logicalhan but what `includeTimings` without `verbose` would return? If it returns the timing of every check, isn't this already verbose?

My thought was that it would individually log out the timing details into kube-apiserver.log. The actual output of healthz would be the same.

> @jpbetz suggested that we return a structured data, with JSON or something (based on the `Accept` header). It is easier and more extensible, I like this approach better.
> 
> One thing that I would prefer is using query parameters instead of Headers, to be easier to use and share with others. Maybe `/healthz?json` or `/healthz?format=json` to be more explicit.
> 
> Suggestion of a possible JSON for this:
> 
> ```js
> {
>     "status" : "healthy", // aggregation of all checks
>     "checks" : [
>         { 
>             "name" : "ping",
>             "status" : "healthy",
>             "duration" : 15 // milliseconds
>             // if unhealthy return a field "reason"
>             // example of values "timeout", "connection failed" or whatever reason.
>         },
>         {
>             "name" : "etcd",
>             "status" : "healthy",
>             "duration" : 27
>         }
>     ]
> }
> ```
> 
> WDYT?

I (and @DirectXMan12) think supporting json format would be super nice (it is an orthogonal issue to this one, however). Also, we should specify the content type through the header and not through query params.

@logicalhan You said it is an orthogonal issue, to clarify that, Do you mean that it should be done in another issue?

I changed my mind and agree with the header instead of query parameter.
Yeah, it's probably a good idea to just split the JSON output to a separate issue

review_comments: I was surprised to see a verbosity level named by a field that is output at that level. Usually verbosity levels are named based on severity (info, warn, error, ...) or numbered (like kube-apiserver has) or some other more general categorization of the level.

An alternative approach might to provide a structured data healthz output (e.g. json) which can safely have fields added to it in a backward compatible way. E.g. the client requests `/healthz` with `Accept: application/json` and the server provides a structured response that can safely include the duration fields (and whatever we choose to add in the future). Client's wouldn't need to figure out how to parse the healthz text response to get machine readable access to the data. Would that be reasonable here?
